content: 1. For cases of food poisoning caused by Bacillus subtilis, the recommended treatment approach is supportive care. This involves managing symptoms and ensuring adequate hydration and electrolyte balance, as the condition is typically self-limiting. 2. For other infections caused by Bacillus subtilis, the preferred treatment regimen includes the use of either vancomycin or clindamycin. These antibiotics are effective against the organism in most cases. 3. If the preferred antibiotics are not suitable or available, alternative treatment options include ciprofloxacin or imipenem. These agents can also provide effective coverage against Bacillus subtilis infections. 4. The above recommendations are supported by authoritative sources, including: Bennett, John (2015). Mandell, Douglas, and Bennett's Principles and Practice of Infectious Diseases. Philadelphia, PA: Elsevier/Saunders. Gilbert, David (2015). The Sanford Guide to Antimicrobial Therapy. Sperryville, VA: Antimicrobial Therapy. ISBN 978-1930808843. Andrews, J., & Wise, R. (2002). Susceptibility testing of Bacillus species. The Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy, 49(6): 1040–1042.
